decisions.question: Gate 1, Echo Well: which concept should go to TRELLIS?
Gate 2, Echo Well: approve a candidate for cooking, regenerate with a new seed, or revise the concept?

Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: the Echo Well, both wagons and the cargo, with vertex data quantized by quantize_static_glb.py before the meshopt step, are in the running game (board 127.0.0.1:47897, _reviews/gate3-static-quantized). Files fall 32.4% (3,835,088 to 2,590,916 bytes) and the gzip download 32.2% (3,647,712 to 2,474,649). In 51 game frames the worst whole-frame mean difference is 0.0077/255 and at most 0.0054% of a frame's pixels change by more than 8/255; programs and draw calls are identical. Should I ship the quantized props?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.

supplementary.question: Gate 3 final approval: ship the line soldier (cook-015) and the Echo Well to main, as shown in the running game (review board _reviews/gate3/board.json and a playable build of the same code)?
supplementary.superseded: Re-shipped meshopt-compressed: the same cook with its vertices and triangles reordered for locality (the same vertex data and triangles, with the same winding) and EXT_meshopt_compression without lossy filters; about a fifth fewer bytes and unchanged in the game (_reviews/gate3-meshopt).

supplementary.question: Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: all 23 shipped models, with their vertices and triangles reordered for locality and their geometry, skin and animation data compressed with EXT_meshopt_compression (no lossy filters), are in the running game (board 127.0.0.1:47896, _reviews/gate3-meshopt). Files fall 19.7% (23,330,396 to 18,733,460 bytes) and the gzip download GitHub Pages serves 6.9% (17,957,653 to 16,725,201 bytes), for 6,117 gzip bytes of decoder. Every model decodes to the same mesh, skin, clips and images; every frame-verifier metric is unchanged; of 213 game frames 200 are bit-identical and 13 differ in one pixel each; shader programs, draw calls (except +1-2 off-screen submissions in three shots), frame times and preload time show no measurable change. Should I ship the compressed models?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.

supplementary.superseded: Re-shipped with quantized vertex data (quantize_static_glb.py: 16-bit positions with one uniform scale per mesh in its node, 8-bit normals and tangents, 16-bit UVs) before the meshopt step; about a third fewer bytes and visually unchanged in the game (_reviews/gate3-static-quantized).
